newsitem.title: BOTSWANA: Canada delivers war planes to Botswana.
newsitem.headline: Canada delivers war planes to Botswana.

text.p: Botswana has received at least one of the Canadian F5 fighter-bombers it ordered in June and more are due to arrive by the end of April, the head of the defence force said on Saturday.

Lieutenant-General Seretse Khama Ian Khama, in a telephone interview, declined to give further details of the deal. "We are not yet ready to talk about the acquisitions... maybe next year when the rest arrive," he said.
A Botswana newspaper on Friday published a picture of President Ketumile Masire climbing into the cockpit of the first F5 to arrive. The paper did not say how many planes had been delivered.
Earlier reports have said Botswana ordered 13 of the aircraft from Canada.
The purchase of the aircraft and an attempt to buy 50 tanks from the Netherlands raised concerns in neighbouring Namibia which has a border dispute with Botswana.
Germany stepped in under NATO rules to thwart the deal to buy tanks from the Netherlands, saying arms should not be sold to southern Africa because tensions were too high in the region.
